title: Throttled fan-out controller and stable fallback matrix (hotpatch)
author: Marina Alvarez
description: Motivation: a recent production incident exposed that immediate fan-out to secondary regions during a primary-region slowdown amplified KV-cache pressure and produced oscillating circuit flips. This PR implements a throttled fan-out controller and a compact fallback matrix to allow staged, predictable degradation instead of blunt failover. Key features: 1) Fan-out controller that applies per-tenant rate envelopes and tokenized fan-out windows to stagger requests to fallback regions and models; 2) Fallback matrix config (runtime and persisted) mapping preferred fallback targets to soft-degradation policies (priority, batch-size caps, kv-preserve hints); 3) Backpressure coordinator that surfaces intent to the SLO enforcer so shedding decisions are coordinated (soft-shed first, circuit only after grace); 4) Canary flags, metrics and histograms for fan-out latency, fallback hit-rate, kv-pressure and tenant-level SLO spend; 5) Safety: feature-flagged rollout, break-glass revert path, and conservative default matrix for tenants with strict SLAs. Rollout plan: staged canary on two dedicated pools (10% traffic) -> expand to 30% with monitoring gates -> enable in hosted with gradient ramp. Revert: feature flag off plus emergency rollout that forcibly drains staggered fan-outs and reverts fallback assignments. Related: ties to incident SUP-4451 postmortem and ENG-2129 design doc. Checklist: - unit+integration tests added; - perf lab run with synthetic spike tests; - console docs and RBAC knobs updated; - SRE runbook updated and pager notified. Why this is different: instead of hard circuit flips we prefer a measurable, meter-driven degradation path that preserves KV caches and avoids cross-region thrash, preserving latency SLOs for high-priority tenants.
commits: Introduce fanout controller and envelope store
Add fallback matrix runtime config and persistence
Hook fallback decisions into SLO enforcer and backpressure coordinator
Telemetry: histograms/gauges for fanout latency and kv pressure
Canary flags, unit tests and integration harness for spike scenarios
review_comments: Ethan Cole: This looks sane; please add an assertion around tenant envelope expiry to avoid stale envelopes causing silent throttles.
Marina Alvarez: Added expiry and a defensive nil-check in envelope_store.go; updated integration test to cover expiry behavior.
Priya Nair: Can we add a dashboard panel for per-tenant fallback hit-rate? SRE wants to watch this during canary.
Marina Alvarez: Added telemetry panel IDs and exported a lightweight aggregated metric (fallback.hit_rate) to Grafana team.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial fail on timing flake -> rerun passed
release_notes: Hotpatch: staged fan-out controller and fallback matrix to reduce cascade overload during regional slowdowns; opt-in via feature flag; SRE rollout required.
notes_for_ops: Turn on feature flag 'hotpatch.fanout_matrix' in dedicated pools first. Watch metrics: telemetry.fanout.latency_p50, telemetry.kv.pressure, fallback.hit_rate. If fallback.hit_rate spikes above expected or kv.pressure increases, flip feature flag off and run emergency drain script deploy/scripts/fanout_drain.sh.
post_deploy_actions: Run synthetic spike tests against canary nodes every 2h for first 12h
Collect debug logs for any tenant that experiences >2x latency regression and open ENG ticket
changelog_summary: Adds throttled fan-out and a fallback mapping to improve graceful degradation during regional slowdowns; feature-flagged and canaried; includes telemetry and revert plan.
